how_to_check: Read age from serial/label; look at tank base, fittings, pan
finding: Water leaking from the tank itself, or rusty water from the tank
customer_message: The tank is failing — leaks get worse fast and can flood the basement.

how_to_check: Same
finding: Gas tank 12+ years old (no leak)
customer_message: Most gas tanks last 8–12 years. Replacing on your schedule avoids an emergency.

how_to_check: Same
finding: Gas tank 10–12 years old, rust on fittings, or popping/rumbling noise
customer_message: Getting near end of life. A flush can extend it; plan for replacement.

how_to_check: Same
finding: Under 10 years, no rust, quiet
customer_message: In good shape.

how_to_check: Look at T&P valve and discharge pipe
finding: T&P valve dripping, or discharge pipe missing/too short
customer_message: The safety valve needs attention to protect against over-pressure.

how_to_check: Look at draft hood/vent; smell for gas; scorch marks
finding: Scorching at burner, vent disconnected, or gas smell
customer_message: Safety risk (carbon monoxide or gas). We need to fix this before it runs again.

how_to_check: Gauge on a hose bib
finding: Over 80 psi (over 100 = RED)
customer_message: High pressure wears out faucets, toilets and the water heater early.

how_to_check: Locate and turn the valve gently
finding: Valve seized or leaks when turned
customer_message: In an emergency you need to be able to shut the water off.

how_to_check: Run every faucet hot and cold; look at spout and handles
finding: Steady drip or handle leak
customer_message: A drip wastes water and gets worse; a cartridge usually fixes it.

how_to_check: Same
finding: Faucet 15+ years old with drip, low flow or corrosion
customer_message: Old faucets are cheaper to replace than to keep repairing.

how_to_check: Look under every sink with a flashlight; feel supply lines
finding: Active leak, water stain that is wet, or swollen cabinet floor
customer_message: Leaks under a sink damage cabinets and floors quickly.

how_to_check: Same
finding: Corroded or crusty angle stops, or old braided lines (10+ yrs)
customer_message: These parts fail without warning; replacing them is cheap insurance.

how_to_check: Flush each; listen for refill; dye test in tank
finding: Runs on its own or keeps refilling
customer_message: A running toilet can waste thousands of gallons a year.

how_to_check: Rock the toilet gently; look at the base
finding: Toilet rocks, or water/stain at the base
recommend: Reset toilet with new wax ring
customer_message: A leaking seal rots the subfloor under the toilet.

how_to_check: Look at tank and bowl
finding: Crack in tank or bowl
customer_message: Cracks can split open and flood the bathroom.

how_to_check: Fill and drain each sink and tub
finding: One slow drain
customer_message: Slow drains turn into clogs.

how_to_check: Same; listen for gurgling; check floor drain
finding: Several slow drains, gurgling, or sewage smell
customer_message: Signs of a main line problem — a backup can put sewage in the basement.

how_to_check: Pour water in pit or lift float; watch it run
finding: Pump does not start
customer_message: Without a working pump the basement can flood in the next storm.

how_to_check: Same; read age
finding: Pump 7+ years old, noisy, or no backup
customer_message: Pumps usually last 7–10 years; replace before it fails.

how_to_check: Run each outside faucet
finding: Leaks, or not frost-free and freezing risk
recommend: Replace with frost-free hose bib (before winter)
customer_message: Old outside faucets can freeze and burst inside the wall.

how_to_check: Look at exposed pipes in basement/utility areas
finding: Galvanized or polybutylene pipe, heavy corrosion
customer_message: This pipe type is past its life; plan a repipe before leaks start.

how_to_check: Run it; look underneath
finding: Leaking from the unit, or jams/hums
customer_message: Leaking disposals cannot be repaired.

how_to_check: Press TEST/RESET on outlets in kitchen, baths, garage, basement, laundry, outside
finding: GFCI does not trip or does not reset
customer_message: This outlet protects against shock near water, and it is not working.

how_to_check: Same
finding: No GFCI where one is required
customer_message: Current code requires shock protection here.

how_to_check: Plug-in tester in a sample of outlets; look and feel
finding: Scorch marks, warm outlet/switch, buzzing, or burning smell
customer_message: Heat at an outlet is a fire warning sign.

how_to_check: Same
finding: Loose outlet (plug falls out), cracked cover, or open ground
customer_message: Loose connections can overheat over time.

how_to_check: Press test on each; read date on back
finding: Alarm does not sound, or no CO alarm in a home with gas
customer_message: Alarms are your first warning in a fire or CO leak.

how_to_check: Same
finding: Alarm 10+ years old
customer_message: Sensors wear out after 10 years even if the test button works.

how_to_check: Remove the panel cover (trained tech, insulated gloves); read panel brand and label
finding: Federal Pacific (Stab-Lok), Zinsco or Challenger panel
customer_message: These panels have a known record of breakers that may not trip.

how_to_check: Cover off: look at breakers, bus, and wiring; smell; infrared thermometer on breakers
finding: Rust or water in/around panel, buzzing, burning smell, hot breaker
customer_message: These are signs of a dangerous connection inside the panel.

how_to_check: Cover off: connections, double taps, aluminum, breaker condition
finding: Double-tapped breakers, melted insulation, loose lugs
customer_message: Found inside the panel — needs correcting for safety.

how_to_check: Read main breaker size
finding: 100A or less and customer plans EV, heat pump or addition
customer_message: Your service may not handle the new load you are planning.

how_to_check: Look for whole-house surge device at panel
finding: None installed
customer_message: Protects the electronics in your HVAC, appliances and TVs.

how_to_check: Ask the member; flick lights
finding: Lights flicker or dim when appliances start
customer_message: Can be a loose connection that needs checking.

how_to_check: Look at meter base, service mast, weatherhead and service entrance cable
finding: Mast leaning, meter base rusted or damaged, cable jacket cracked, water entry at weatherhead
recommend: Repair or replace meter base / service entrance cable (utility coordinates disconnect)
customer_message: Damaged service equipment lets water in — a shock and fire risk, and the utility may refuse to reconnect after a storm.

how_to_check: Look at exposed wiring in basement/attic
finding: Knob-and-tube or aluminum branch wiring
customer_message: Older wiring types need an electrician to check they are safe.

how_to_check: Pull the filter
finding: Dirty filter
customer_message: Included in your membership.

how_to_check: CO meter near furnace and in living area
finding: Any CO reading above 9 ppm in the living area
recommend: Shut off furnace, open windows, HVAC tech today
customer_message: Carbon monoxide is dangerous — we must find the source now.

how_to_check: Watch flame when blower starts; look at heat exchanger area and flue
finding: Flame rolls or changes when blower starts, rust-through, disconnected flue
customer_message: Signs of a cracked heat exchanger or venting problem — a CO risk.

how_to_check: Read age from label
finding: Furnace 20+ years old
customer_message: Past normal life — replacing on your schedule avoids a winter breakdown.

how_to_check: Same
finding: Furnace 15–20 years old
customer_message: Getting near end of life; start planning.

how_to_check: HVAC tech: flame sensor microamps, igniter condition
finding: Weak flame signal or cracked igniter
customer_message: These parts cause no-heat calls on cold nights.

how_to_check: Look at drain line, pan, float switch
finding: Water in pan, clogged drain, no float switch
customer_message: A clogged drain can overflow and damage ceilings or floors.

how_to_check: Thermometer at return and supply while cooling
finding: Temperature drop under 14°F or over 22°F
customer_message: The system is not cooling efficiently; needs a closer look.

how_to_check: Look at coil, fins, clearance, disconnect
finding: Coil blocked with debris, fins crushed, plants within 2 ft
customer_message: Keeping the unit clear helps it run efficiently.

how_to_check: HVAC tech: capacitor µF test, contactor look
finding: Capacitor bulging/leaking or out of rating
customer_message: A failing capacitor can leave you with no AC in a heat wave.

how_to_check: Same
finding: Contactor pitted or burnt
customer_message: Worn contacts can damage the compressor.

how_to_check: Read label: refrigerant type and age
finding: R-22 system, or AC 15+ years old
customer_message: R-22 is no longer made — repairs get very expensive.

how_to_check: Same
finding: AC 12–15 years with repairs in the last 2 years
customer_message: Near end of life; repair money is better put toward a new unit.

how_to_check: Check it holds setpoint; look at type
finding: Not holding temperature, or old mercury/manual thermostat
customer_message: A programmable thermostat saves on energy bills.

how_to_check: Listen at air handler while running
finding: Squeal, grinding, or motor very hot
customer_message: Motor noise usually means bearings are failing.

how_to_check: Look at accessible ductwork
finding: Disconnected or crushed duct, or major gaps
customer_message: You are paying to heat/cool the basement or attic.

how_to_check: Same
finding: Service entrance cable original to a pre-1980 home, or undersized for a planned upgrade
recommend: Plan service upgrade with new service cable
customer_message: Old service cable is a common failure point; replacing it with an upgrade avoids an emergency.
